criterion: The NAT-020 loader, started from the RECOVERY slot with visible stage markers, reaches its memory preparation, ADT/boot_args and pre-jump stages on the S24 (CRC-valid STAGE frames MAIN, FB, MEM, ZERO, COPY, ADT, CLEAN, PRE_JUMP decoded from an independent recording).
summary: One native run of NAT-022 loader-diag-trig-hold-adt8 (RECOVERY image sha256 38411cd82af4ae4b68079472d68936c23b3877208f301f33c295741ae991ce38, Image.payload 766218b288b3fddaef79d7347f91b57aab5f7329e4d574389eb142226726a87a, loader Image 901565b2..., source commit 1092fab). It was written to RECOVERY (/dev/block/sda18) with a matching full readback and booted once (adb reboot recovery at 2026-11-10T15:28:40.9Z). The owner filmed the screen (84.7 s recording). decode_video.py decoded 781 CRC-valid frames. The recording shows the loader stage markers MAIN (0x20), FB (0x21), MEM (0x30, ~8 s), ZERO (0x31), COPY (0x32), then an exception report from inside the loader: STAGE 0x1f, STAGE idx1 reached-stage mask 0x003f (ENTRY..COPY; ADT/CLEAN/PRE_JUMP not reached), SLOT 4, ESR 0x96000061 (EC 0x25 data abort without a change of EL, DFSC 0x21 alignment fault, WnR 1), ELR 0x800a9954, FAR 0x00000009e2d743fc, then the DECON0 REG report (status 1, GLOBAL_CON 0x0133, TRIG_CON 0x3062->0x3063, FRAME_COUNT 0x0686->0x0687, kick count 0x0f). The exception cycle repeats every ~29.8 s (seen three times) with the same values; the frame counter advances ~60 Hz. No ADT, CLEAN or PRE_JUMP marker and no XNU entry marker was shown. Host analysis (not a device observation): the loader runs at image base 0x800a0000 (ELR minus the code offset in the flashed loader); ELR is `stur x19, [x11, #0x24]` in adt_set_dram (adt_patch.c writing the 64-bit `dram-size` value); FAR minus 1020 = 0x9e2d74000 is the 16 KiB-aligned ADT copy, value offset 1020 = 4-byte aligned only. The loader runs with the MMU off (data accesses are Device memory and must be naturally aligned), so the 64-bit store to a 4-byte-aligned address faults. The earlier host pre-check (NAT-026) ran adt_patch.c on x86-64, which tolerates misaligned accesses, and was blind to this. Stock RECOVERY was restored with one NAT-013 session in Download Mode (host observer saw 04e8:685d at 15:30:36Z; restore 15:33:10Z-15:33:14Z; Android back 15:33:59Z); hash equals stock 96620b8b..., check_android pass, Android booted.

established: The NAT-020 loader ran on the S24 from the RECOVERY slot at image base 0x800a0000 (S-Boot places a RECOVERY Image at a base that varies by image: 0x801a0000 for the canary image of run 003) and its own markers MAIN, FB, MEM, ZERO and COPY were drawn and decoded from an independent recording: FDT parsing, RAM-window choice, zeroing of the window (~7-8 s) and the copy of all 10 payload segments (21.5 MB) completed.

The loader then took a synchronous data abort in the ADT patch stage (SLOT 4, ESR 0x96000061 = alignment fault on a store, ELR 0x800a9954, FAR 0x9e2d743fc). The exception record was reported from inside the loader on the framebuffer, with stage, ESR, ELR and FAR decoded from the recording (goal step 5 met for the loader).

The failing instruction and cause are identified on the host by two independent routes (ELR + disassembly; FAR - 1020 = 16 KiB-aligned ADT base + dram-size value offset): a 64-bit store to a 4-byte-aligned ADT property value with the MMU off.
The exception reporting path keeps the display updating: DECON0 status 1, FRAME_COUNT advancing at ~60 Hz across 29.8 s cycles, kick counter rising 0x0f -> 0x27.
The run-004 payload-header failure is fixed: the loader now passes the payload header, FDT, RAM-window, zero and copy stages.
